```{r}
# VIF Fremoval
remove_highest_vif <- function(model, threshold = 2.5, return_model = TRUE) {
  require(car)
  gvif_df <- car::vif(model)
  max_vif <- max(gvif_df[, 3])
  
  if (max_vif <= threshold) {
    message("No variables exceed the VIF threshold of ", threshold)
    return(model)
  }
  
  highest_idx <- which.max(gvif_df[, 3])
  highest_var <- rownames(gvif_df)[highest_idx]
  
  cat(paste0("Removing: ", highest_var, 
             " (GVIF = ", round(gvif_df[highest_idx, 1], 4), 
             ", GVIF^(1/(2*Df)) = ", round(gvif_df[highest_idx, 3], 4), ")\n"))
  
  formula_updated <- update(formula(model), paste(". ~ . -", highest_var))
  
  if (return_model) {
    return(update(model, formula_updated))
  } else {
    return(formula_updated)
  }
}

full_model <- full_model_raw
threshold <- 5

while (TRUE) {
 vif_results <- car::vif(full_model)
 if (max(vif_results[, 3]) <= threshold) {
   cat("All variables now have VIF below", threshold, "\n")
   break
 }
 full_model <- remove_highest_vif(full_model, threshold = threshold)
}
```

```{r}
# Stepwise forward selection using AIC
aic_forward_model <- suppressWarnings(stepAIC(null_model, 
                         scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                         direction = "forward", 
                         trace = FALSE))

# Stepwise backward selection using AIC
aic_backward_model <- suppressWarnings(stepAIC(full_model, 
                         scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                         direction = "backward", 
                         trace = FALSE))

# Stepwise both selection using AIC
aic_both_model <- suppressWarnings(stepAIC(null_model, 
                         scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                         direction = "both", 
                         trace = FALSE))

# Stepwise forward selection using BIC
bic_forward_model <- suppressWarnings(stepAIC(null_model, 
                       scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                       direction = "forward", 
                       k = log(nrow(model.frame(null_model))),
                       trace = FALSE))

# Stepwise backward selection using BIC
bic_backward_model <- suppressWarnings(stepAIC(full_model, 
                        scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                        direction = "backward", 
                        k = log(nrow(model.frame(null_model))),
                        trace = FALSE))

# Stepwise both selection using BIC
bic_both_model <- suppressWarnings(stepAIC(null_model, 
                    scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                    direction = "both", 
                    k = log(nrow(model.frame(null_model))),
                    trace = FALSE))
```

```{r}
# Create CV folds
set.seed(123)
fold_indices <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(train_data)))

# Create full model matrix first
x_full <- model.matrix(is_sleep_deprived ~ ., train_data)[,-1]
y_full <- train_data$is_sleep_deprived

# Run CV directly
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x_full, y_full, alpha=1, 
                     family="binomial", weights=weights_vector,
                     foldid=fold_indices, type.measure="deviance")

# Get best lambda
best_lambda <- cv_lasso$lambda.min

# Final model with optimal lambda
final_lasso <- glmnet(x_full, y_full, alpha=1, 
                     lambda=best_lambda, family="binomial", 
                     weights=weights_vector)

x_full <- model.matrix(is_sleep_deprived ~ ., train_data)[,-1]
y_full <- train_data$is_sleep_deprived
set.seed(123)
fold_indices <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(train_data)))

# Ridge regression (alpha=0)
cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x_full, y_full, alpha=0, 
                    family="binomial", weights=weights_vector,
                    foldid=fold_indices, type.measure="deviance")
best_lambda_ridge <- cv_ridge$lambda.min
final_ridge <- glmnet(x_full, y_full, alpha=0, 
                    lambda=best_lambda_ridge, family="binomial", 
                    weights=weights_vector)


# Setup for tuning alpha and lambda together
x_full <- model.matrix(is_sleep_deprived ~ ., train_data)[,-1]
y_full <- train_data$is_sleep_deprived
set.seed(123)
fold_indices <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(train_data)))

# Define grid of alpha values to try
alpha_grid <- seq(0, 1, by=0.1)
cv_results <- list()
best_cvm <- Inf
best_alpha <- NULL
best_lambda <- NULL

# Tune alpha and lambda together
for (a in alpha_grid) {
 cv_model <- cv.glmnet(x_full, y_full, alpha=a, 
                      family="binomial", weights=weights_vector,
                      foldid=fold_indices, type.measure="deviance")
 
 cv_results[[as.character(a)]] <- cv_model
 
 if (min(cv_model$cvm) < best_cvm) {
   best_cvm <- min(cv_model$cvm)
   best_alpha <- a
   best_lambda <- cv_model$lambda.min
 }
}

# Final model with optimal parameters
final_elastic <- glmnet(x_full, y_full, alpha=best_alpha, 
                      lambda=best_lambda, family="binomial", 
                      weights=weights_vector)

```

```{r}
  Best_Parameters = c("", "", "", "", "", "",
                     paste("lambda =", round(best_lambda, 5)),
                     paste("lambda =", round(best_lambda_ridge, 5)),
                     paste("alpha =", best_alpha, ", lambda =", round(best_lambda, 5)))
)

# Print updated summary table
print(model_summary)
```

```{r}
# Helper function to compute metrics
get_metrics <- function(model, data, y_true) {
  prob <- predict(model, newdata = data, type = "response")
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0,1))
  
  auc  <- roc(y_true, prob, quiet = TRUE)$auc
  cm   <- confusionMatrix(pred, factor(y_true, levels = c(0,1)), positive = "1")
  
  c(
    AUC         = as.numeric(auc),
    F1          = as.numeric(cm$byClass["F1"]),
    Accuracy    = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Sensitivity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"])
  )
}

# For LASSO, Ridge, Elastic Net (predict differently!)
get_metrics_glmnet <- function(model, x, y_true) {
  prob <- predict(model, newx = x, type = "response")[,1]
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0,1))
  
  auc  <- roc(y_true, prob, quiet = TRUE)$auc
  cm   <- confusionMatrix(pred, factor(y_true, levels = c(0,1)), positive = "1")
  
  c(
    AUC         = as.numeric(auc),
    F1          = as.numeric(cm$byClass["F1"]),
    Accuracy    = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Sensitivity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"])
  )
}

# --- make test design matrix match the training matrix -----------------------
# build raw matrix
x_test <- model.matrix(~ ., data = X_test)[, -1]
# add any columns seen in training but absent in test (fill with 0)
missing_cols <- setdiff(colnames(x_full), colnames(x_test))
if (length(missing_cols)) {
  x_test <- cbind(
    x_test,
    matrix(0, nrow(x_test), length(missing_cols),
           dimnames = list(NULL, missing_cols))
  )
}
# drop extras and reorder to match training
x_test <- x_test[, colnames(x_full), drop = FALSE]

# --- Count original variables instead of encoded features ---
# Function to count original variables from a model
count_original_variables <- function(model) {
  # Extract variable names from the model formula
  if ("terms" %in% names(model)) {
    var_names <- all.vars(formula(model)[-2])  # Exclude response variable
    return(length(var_names))
  } else if (class(model)[1] == "glmnet") {
    # For glmnet models, we need to count differently
    # This depends on how you set up your data, adjust as needed
    # Assuming you have the original variable names stored somewhere
    return(length(unique(gsub("_.*$", "", colnames(model$beta)))))
  }
  return(NA)  # Return NA if can't determine
}

# --- compute performance metrics for every model ---
metrics_list <- list(
  # get_metrics(full_model,  X_test, y_test),
  # get_metrics(null_model,  X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics(aic_forward_model,  X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics(aic_backward_model, X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics(aic_both_model,     X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics(bic_forward_model,  X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics(bic_backward_model, X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics(bic_both_model,     X_test, y_test),
  get_metrics_glmnet(final_lasso,   x_test, y_test),
  get_metrics_glmnet(final_ridge,   x_test, y_test),
  get_metrics_glmnet(final_elastic, x_test, y_test)
)



# Update model_summary with both variables and features
model_list <- list(
  aic_forward_model, aic_backward_model, aic_both_model,
  bic_forward_model, bic_backward_model, bic_both_model,
  final_lasso, final_ridge, final_elastic
)

# Keep the existing Features column (rename it)
model_summary$Features <- model_summary$Variables

# Add new Variables column with original variable counts
model_summary$Variables <- sapply(model_list, count_original_variables)

# Reorder columns to put Variables before Features
col_order <- c("Model", "Variables", "Features", "Best_Parameters")
model_summary <- model_summary[, c(col_order, setdiff(names(model_summary), col_order))]

# bind rows → data-frame, then attach to summary table
metrics_df <- do.call(rbind, metrics_list)
model_summary <- cbind(model_summary, as.data.frame(metrics_df))
print(model_summary)
```

```{r}
# Create a larger deviance residuals plot
par(mfrow=c(1,1), mar=c(5,5,4,2), cex=1.2)

dev_res <- residuals(bic_forward_model, type = "deviance")
plot(predict(bic_forward_model), dev_res,
    xlab = "Linear predictor", ylab = "Deviance residuals",
    main = "Deviance residuals vs fitted values",
    pch=19, cex=0.7)  # Solid points, slightly smaller for clarity
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

# Add smoother line with wider span to see general trend
smoothed <- loess(dev_res ~ predict(bic_forward_model), span=0.75)
ord <- order(predict(bic_forward_model))
lines(predict(bic_forward_model)[ord], predict(smoothed)[ord], 
     col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
# Extract just the needed columns from each dataset for the analysis
train_subset <- data.frame(
  sleep_hour = as.numeric(as.character(train_data$sleep_time_weekdays_cat)),
  is_sleep_deprived = train_data$is_sleep_deprived
)
test_subset <- data.frame(
  sleep_hour = as.numeric(as.character(test_data$sleep_time_weekdays_cat)),
  is_sleep_deprived = test_data$is_sleep_deprived
)
# Combine the subsets with only needed columns
combined_subset <- rbind(train_subset, test_subset)
# Aggregate data: calculate proportion of deprived by hour
sleep_stats <- aggregate(
  is_sleep_deprived ~ sleep_hour, 
  data = combined_subset,
  FUN = function(x) c(prop = mean(x), count = length(x))
)
# Convert to data frame with proper columns
sleep_stats_df <- data.frame(
  hour = sleep_stats$sleep_hour,
  prop_deprived = sleep_stats$is_sleep_deprived[,1],
  count = sleep_stats$is_sleep_deprived[,2]
)
# Sort by hour for proper display
sleep_stats_df <- sleep_stats_df[order(sleep_stats_df$hour),]
ggplot(sleep_stats_df) +
  # Primary bars for proportion
  geom_bar(aes(x = factor(hour), y = prop_deprived), 
           fill = "#1d4f30", stat = "identity") +
  # Secondary axis for count
  geom_line(aes(x = factor(hour), y = count/max(count), group = 1), 
            color = "red", size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  # geom_point(aes(x = factor(hour), y = count/max(count)), 
  #            color = "darkred", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Set up dual axis with simplified scale
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "% Deprived",
    limits = c(0, 1), 
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~.*max(sleep_stats_df$count), 
                        name = "Sample Count", 
                        breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(sleep_stats_df$count)/1000)*1000, 1000))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Deprived by Sleeping Start Hour",
    x = "Sleep Start Hour"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
```

```{r}
get_metrics_at_thresholds <- function(model, data, y_true, thresholds) {
  prob <- predict(model, newdata = data, type = "response")
  auc <- roc(y_true, prob, quiet = TRUE)$auc
  
  results <- data.frame()
  for (t in thresholds) {
    pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > t, 1, 0), levels = c(0,1))
    cm <- confusionMatrix(pred, factor(y_true, levels = c(0,1)), positive = "1")
    
    # Calculate actual prevalence from the data
    prevalence <- sum(y_true == 1) / length(y_true)
    
    # Calculate percentage flagged as positive
    true_pos_rate <- as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"])
    precision <- as.numeric(cm$byClass["Precision"])
    true_positives <- true_pos_rate * prevalence
    false_positives <- true_positives * (1/precision - 1)
    percent_flagged <- (true_positives + false_positives) * 100
    
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
      Threshold = t,
      Precision = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Precision"]),
      Recall = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
      F1 = as.numeric(cm$byClass["F1"]),
      Accuracy = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
      # AUC = auc,
      PercentFlagged = percent_flagged
    ))
  }
  return(results)
}

# Create threshold table for BIC Forward Selection
thresholds <- seq(0.15, 0.6, by = 0.05)
bic_forward_thresholds <- get_metrics_at_thresholds(
  bic_forward_model, X_test, y_test, thresholds
)

# Print formatted results
print(bic_forward_thresholds, digits = 4)
```
```{r}
cv_results <- data.frame(Fold = 1:k, Sensitivity = NA, Precision = NA, F1 = NA, AUC = NA)
for (i in 1:k) {
  # Get validation fold
  valid_fold <- train_data[folds == i, ]
  
  # Get predictions
  prob <- predict(bic_forward_model, newdata = valid_fold, type = "response")
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0,1))
  
  # Calculate metrics
  auc <- roc(valid_fold$is_sleep_deprived, prob, quiet = TRUE)$auc
  cm <- confusionMatrix(pred, factor(valid_fold$is_sleep_deprived, levels = c(0,1)), positive = "1")
  
  # Store results
  cv_results$Sensitivity[i] <- cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]
  cv_results$Precision[i] <- cm$byClass["Precision"]
  cv_results$F1[i] <- cm$byClass["F1"]
  cv_results$AUC[i] <- auc
}

# Calculate average and standard deviation
cv_results <- rbind(
  cv_results,
  data.frame(
    Fold = "Average", 
    Sensitivity = mean(cv_results$Sensitivity), 
    Precision = mean(cv_results$Precision),
    F1 = mean(cv_results$F1),
    AUC = mean(cv_results$AUC)
  ),
  data.frame(
    Fold = "Standard Deviation", 
    Sensitivity = sd(cv_results$Sensitivity), 
    Precision = sd(cv_results$Precision),
    F1 = sd(cv_results$F1),
    AUC = sd(cv_results$AUC)
  )
)
print(cv_results)
```

```{r}
# Calculate percentages by weekday_sleep_timing and gender
summary_data <- train_data %>%
  group_by(weekday_sleep_timing, gender) %>%

    n = n(),
    pct_deprived = mean(is_sleep_deprived) * 100,
    .groups = 'drop'

# Create the plot with theme matching your slides
ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = weekday_sleep_timing, y = pct_deprived, fill = gender)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.8) +
  # Percentages - all in black and rounded to whole numbers
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_deprived, 0), "%")), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            vjust = -0.5, 
            size = 3.5,
            color = "black") +
  # Sample sizes - conditionally colored
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n=", n), 
                color = gender == "Male"), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            vjust = 2, 
            size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "black", "TRUE" = "white"), guide = "none") +
  # Using a dark green/gray color scheme to match your example slides
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Female" = "#cccccc", "Male" = "#1d4f30")) +
  labs(
    title = "Interaction: weekday_sleep_timing × Gender → Sleep Deprivation",
    x = "",
    y = "% Sleep Deprived",
    fill = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  ylim(0, 100)  # Set y-axis from 0 to 100%
```
